# Emiliano Rizza

<div class="subtitle">
Theoretical Physics PhD Researcher · Quantum Information · Holography · Spectral Methods · Scientific Computing
</div>

<div class="tagline">
I am a PhD researcher at Jagiellonian University in Kraków, working at the intersection of quantum information, holography, mathematical physics and quantum dynamics. My research asks how thermal and spectral data encode black-hole dynamics, complexity and bulk geometry.
</div>

## Research at a glance

::: {.section-grid}
::: {.card-lite}
### Krylov complexity & holography
Boundary reconstruction from partition functions, BTZ black holes, DSSYK and candidate bulk observables for quantum complexity.
:::

::: {.card-lite}
### Black-hole information
Rényi second laws, charged AdS black holes and information-theoretic constraints on gravitational processes.
:::

::: {.card-lite}
### Spectral & asymptotic methods
Orthogonal polynomials, recurrence coefficients, spectral measures, large deviations and random-matrix-inspired techniques.
:::

::: {.card-lite}
### Scientific computing
Analytical modelling combined with symbolic and numerical workflows, primarily in Wolfram Mathematica and Python.
:::
:::

## Current focus

My recent work develops a partition-function route to Krylov dynamics and investigates how the resulting boundary behavior can be represented geometrically in the bulk. I am also working on analytical spectral reconstruction methods and on information-theoretic constraints for charged AdS black holes.

::: {.callout-note}
I expect to complete my PhD in 2027 and am interested in research opportunities in academia, scientific R&D, quantum technologies and quantitative modelling.
:::
